request.spec:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The header shows the signed-in user's crew total when a person with the user's name leads a
crew: the due-totals of the crews they lead, added up; nothing otherwise.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The header now has a "My crews' due" figure (`my-crew-due-total`). If the signed-in user matches a person on the sheet, by name or alias, it adds up the due-totals of every crew that person leads. If no person matches, or the person leads no crew, it's blank. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

This was a front-end change only; the server and stored data didn't need to change. The edits:
- **`core/crews.ts`**: a new shared helper, `crewDueCents`, works out one crew's due-total (the lead's plus the members' due-totals).
- **`features/crews/crews.ts`**: the crew list now uses that helper, so each crew row and the header figure always agree.
- **`features/people/people.ts`**: a new `myCrewDueTotal` finds the signed-in user's person (the same match "My due" uses), takes the crews they lead and passes the sum to the header.
- **`features/header/header.ts`**: shows the new figure under "My overdue".
